info.title: damrs API
info.description: Digital asset management: ingest, search, rights, provenance.

delete.summary:
Revokes a share. Takes effect on URLs the share already minted, because the share id is in their
signatures and delivery re-checks it on every request.

204.description: Revoked, or already was — revocation is idempotent

403.description: Authenticated, and holds no manage scope

AmendRequest.description: What to change. An omitted member is left alone; `search_alias: null` clears it.

search_alias.description:
Doubly optional: absent leaves the alias alone, `null` removes it. Those are different intents and
a single `Option` cannot express both.

AmendTypeRequest.description:
What to change about a type. An omitted member is left alone.

`field_keys` replaces the list wholesale rather than merging: a type's fields are an ordered list, and
"add this one" computed against a client's stale copy would silently drop whatever it had not seen.

assets_now_incomplete.description: How many live assets would now fail a metadata write for want of a newly-required value.

reindex_required.description: Whether the search index is now stale and needs rebuilding.

AmendedField.description: An amended field, with the consequences of the amendment.

content_hash.description: BLAKE3 of the original bytes, lowercase hex. What deduplication and integrity both key on.

legal_hold.description:
Blocks tiering *and* deletion. Surfaced because a user who cannot delete an asset deserves to know
why rather than to see a failing button.

preview_url.description:
A signed internal-preview URL for the `preview-1024` rendition, when one has been rendered.

On the detail endpoint only. A list of sixty of these would mint sixty tokens for images no grid draws —
the grid uses the thumbnail — and a lightbox opens one asset at a time.

`Contain`-fitted rather than cropped, which is what makes it the right image for somebody inspecting an
asset: the thumbnail is a 256px square crop, so enlarging it is a blurry crop of the wrong aspect.

technical.description:
Probed technical facts — EXIF, codec, colour. Read-only, and shaped by the file rather than by the
tenant's schema, so it is not merged into `values`.

values.description: The validated metadata, keyed by field definition key.

AssetDetail.description: One asset in full, as the detail panel draws it.

AssetPage.description:
One page of results.

`total` is separate from `items.len()` and load-bearing for accessibility: a virtualised grid must
report the real row count in `aria-rowcount`, or a screen reader announces "20 items" for a library
of a hundred thousand.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first item in `items` within the full result set.

total.description: Total matching assets, not the number returned.

AssetSummary.description:
One asset, as the grid renders it.

Deliberately small. A 100k-row grid fetches pages of these, so every field here is multiplied by
the page size — and anything a cell does not draw belongs on the detail endpoint instead.

filename.description: The name the uploader gave it, preserved verbatim. The stored MIME is sniffed, not this.

mime.description: Sniffed on ingest, never taken from the client (`assets.mime`).

rights_state.description:
Rights evaluation outcome. A *display* input: enforcement happens at the distribution
chokepoint (D12), and this field is what dims a button rather than what protects an asset.

tag_confidence.description:
Model confidence in the asset's automatic tags, 0..1. `None` means nothing scored it — which
is not the same as zero, and the UI renders it differently.

thumbnail_url.description:
URL of the thumbnail, as a signed internal-preview delivery URL.

Absolute when the deployment configures `server.public_url`, root-relative otherwise — so a client on a
different origin must resolve it against the API's base rather than its own. Absent when the asset has
no thumbnail yet, which is the normal state between an upload finishing and the worker deriving it: a
URL minted regardless would 404, and a grid cannot tell a broken link from work still in progress.

tier.description:
Where the original lives, derived server-side from storage class and restore state so the UI
never reimplements that mapping.

width.description:
Display dimensions — orientation already applied, so a grid cell can lay out from these
without knowing about EXIF. `None` for formats with no intrinsic size.

AssetTier.description:
The tier a user sees.

Derived from two independent columns — the object's storage class and the state of any restore —
and derived **here** rather than in the UI, because the mapping contains a trap: a restore does not
change an object's storage class, so an *expired* restore of an archived object is archived again.
The schema says so twice, and reimplementing the rule in TypeScript is how a download button stays
enabled until the day someone presses it.

AssetTypeView.description: Which type an asset has, and the form that follows from it.

field_keys.description:
The fields that apply *now*, in order — the resolved answer rather than the stored pointer, because
this is what the client has to draw.

metadata_type_id.description:
`None` means the asset falls back — to the tenant's default type, or to the whole vocabulary when
there is no default. Either way it still has a form; see `dam_db::metadata_types`.

id.description:
A stable identifier where one exists — a taxonomy term id. Absent for a metadata value, whose identity
*is* its text.

value.description:
The value as text. A number or a boolean is rendered rather than typed, because a rail displays it and
the round trip back into a query goes through the field's kind anyway.

BulkFailure.description: One failed row, for the report.

out_of_scope.description:
How many of the submitted ids fell out of scope. Reported as a count and nothing more: which ones,
and whether they exist at all, is exactly what §7 says a caller must not learn.

sample.description: A sample of the targets, for a dialog to name a few rather than list thousands.

target_count.description:
How many assets the operation would touch — after the caller's own scope is applied, so it is the
number that will actually be touched.

asset_ids.description: The selection. Deduplicated server-side; ids the caller may not manage fall out silently.

params.description:
Kind-specific parameters — for `metadata_set`, `{ "values": { … } }` with the same patch semantics
as the single-asset endpoint: `null` clears, absent leaves alone.

BulkStatus.description: An operation as the UI polls it.

failures.description: The first failures, row by row — "must report exactly which rows did not apply".

terminal.description: Whether the state is final, so a client polls this instead of re-implementing the state vocabulary.

CreatedShare.description: A created share. The token appears here and nowhere else, exactly like an issued API key.

portal_path.description: The path a recipient opens, for the client to compose onto its own origin.

token.description:
The one-time token. The table holds a digest, so a lost link cannot be recovered — revoke and
re-create, which is the same posture as an API key and for the same reason.

DefineRequest.description: A field to define. Flags default to the conservative reading when omitted.

searchable.description: Defaults to true: a field nobody can search for is the surprising choice, not the safe one.

Facet.description: One facetable field and its buckets.

truncated.description: Whether buckets were dropped by the limit. Reported rather than left implicit — see [`FACET_BUCKETS`].

FieldDefinition.description: One field definition, as a form needs it.

ai_writable.description: Whether an enrichment run may write it.

kind.description: The database spelling of the kind, so a client can pick an input type.

label.description: The tenant's own label. A form shows this rather than the key.

multivalued.description:
Whether the field takes an array.

Load-bearing rather than informational: a client that does not know this sends a comma-joined string
to a field that takes an array, and the server refuses it with a message about delimiters that the
user cannot act on. Discovered exactly that way, editing a multivalued field in a real browser.

read_only.description: Set by ingest or by a connector; an editor must not offer it.

search_alias.description: The shorthand prefix, when the tenant defined one: `bra:acme` for `brand`.

LatencyClass.description:
How long a `GET` takes to become possible.

The download path and the UI branch on **this**, not on the provider name. That is
what lets Azure Archive or LTO tape slot in later without special-casing (§6.1).

MetadataAccepted.description: The outcome of a metadata edit.

values.description:
The stored document after the merge, so a client does not have to guess what the validator
normalised — a date reformatted or a number coerced would otherwise show up as an unexplained diff
on the next read.

MetadataPatch.description: A metadata edit: the fields to change, keyed by definition key.

values.description:
A merge, not a replacement. `null` for a value clears that field; a key that is absent is left
alone. Two clients editing different fields of one asset must not overwrite each other, and a PUT of
the whole document guarantees they do.

MetadataTypeRow.description: A metadata type, with the count that decides whether editing it is safe.

applies_to.description: The media classes this type is the natural choice for at ingest.

assets.description:
How many live assets currently carry this type.

On the row for the same reason a field's usage count is: removing a type re-forms every asset that
referenced it, and an administrator should not have to go and ask how many that is.

field_keys.description: Its fields, in its own order.

OrderRequest.description: The complete field order, in the order fields should appear.

PlacementState.description:
Lifecycle state of one `object_placements` row.

Mirrors the `object_placements.state` CHECK. In `dam-core` rather than `dam-store`
because both the database layer that loads it and the resolution layer that acts on it
need the same vocabulary — and a second definition is how the two drift.

Only `Present` is readable. The others each mean something different to an operator,
which is why this is not a boolean: `Uploading` will resolve itself, `Missing` needs a
re-replication, `Corrupt` needs a scrub, and `Deleting` is expected to disappear.

url.description: A short-lived delivery URL. Fetch it promptly; the token, not this URL, is what the recipient keeps.

PortalRequest.description:
What a recipient sends. POST rather than GET even for the first look, so the passcode travels in a body —
a passcode in a query string is a passcode in every proxy log on the path.

preview_unavailable.description: Why there is no preview, when there is a stateable reason.

preview_url.description:
A short-lived delivery URL for the web rendition — a full rights-checked distribution, `None` when
rights refuse or no rendition exists yet. The share existing does not entitle anyone to pixels.

ProvenanceState.description:
Content-credential verification outcome. Mirrors the `assets.provenance_state` CHECK.

Four states rather than a boolean because they call for different responses: `None` is a file that
never had a credential, `Invalid` is one whose credential no longer matches its bytes, and
`Untrusted` is an intact credential from a signer outside any trust list. Collapsing them loses
the distinction between "no claim was made" and "a claim was made and broken".

QueryProblem.description: Where a query was refused, so a UI can point at the character.

at.description:
One-based column the parser stopped at, when it has one. A filter rail underlines from here; without it
a user gets "invalid query" and no idea which word.

code.description:
A stable machine-readable code, when the parser gave one. A UI maps it to a message in the user's
language, which prose cannot be.

assets_with_values.description:
How many assets still carry a value under this key. The values are **kept** — see `dam_db`'s
`fields::remove` — so this is what has gone invisible, not what was destroyed.

RestoreState.description: Where a restore has got to, matching `object_placements.restore_state`.

RestoreTier.description: Retrieval speed for a restore, matching `restore_requests.tier`.

RightsState.description: Rights evaluation outcome for an asset. Mirrors the `assets.rights_state` CHECK.

SchemaField.description: A field definition with the numbers an administrator needs before touching it.

assets_with_values.description:
How many live assets carry a value under this key.

The number that decides whether an edit is safe, so it is on the row rather than behind another
request: an administrator deciding whether to remove a field should not have to go and ask.

SetAssetTypeRequest.description: What to set an asset's type to. `null` clears it, which is different from omitting the member.

ShareRequest.description: What a client asks for when sharing an asset.

allow_original.description: Whether the recipient may fetch the original, rather than only the web rendition.

expires_in_hours.description: Hours until the link stops working. Absent means no expiry — revocation is then the only way it ends.

passcode.description: Plaintext; hashed with argon2id server-side and never stored or returned.

ShareRow.description: One row in the management list.

live.description: Whether the link still works, so the list does not make a reader re-derive it from four columns.

SortOrder.description:
The orders a client may ask for.

A closed set on the wire as well as in SQL. Accepting a column name would make the ORDER BY
caller-supplied, and validating one against a list is the same list written twice.

ValidationProblem.description: Why an edit was refused, field by field.

code.description:
A stable machine-readable code. Stable because a client branches on it and a UI maps it to a message
in the user's language, neither of which can be done with prose.

key.description: The payload key, or the field key for a missing required field.
